question: Can I euthanize my cat that has cancer, and will I be with it in Jannah?
asked: My cat has been diagnosed with a type of cancer, and the vets are saying to euthanize him for his own good. I love him a lot and I want to be with him in Jannah, but I also want what is best for him. Am I allowed to euthanize him, and will I be with my cat in Jannah?
answer:
So our sister is asking the painful question of euthanization, and then the theological question about Jannah and pets in Jannah.

The response to this question is that it is completely forbidden in Islam to torture animals for no reason. It is haram, it is sinful, to torture animals for no reason. We all know the hadith of the lady who went to Jahannam because she starved her cat to death, for no reason other than that she was a nasty person. And our Prophet ﷺ cursed the one who tortures an animal. Our Prophet ﷺ said that anyone who takes an animal as target practice, this is something that is sinful and haram. We do not tie up an animal, or do as is done in some countries, where they have a bullfight and kill the animal for entertainment. This is completely haram, and it is one of the major sins of Islam.

And our Prophet ﷺ said, and the hadith is in Nasa'i, that whoever kills even a small chick, a little bird, even a small bird, much less a bigger animal, without just cause, Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala will question him about that on the Day of Judgment. It's a threat that he will have to answer to Allah directly for killing an animal without any just cause. They said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is a just cause?" He said that if he wants to eat an animal, he may sacrifice it and then eat it; he should not just kill it and then leave it on the side of the road for entertainment. That's not something that is allowed. So the hadith is very clear that for any animal that you're going to kill, there must be a reason to kill it.

Based on this: you are saying that your cat is suffering, is going to die a very slow and miserable death because of cancer, and the doctors are saying to euthanize it. In this case there is a reason. You are not torturing; you are not wanting to inflict pain. **The sanctity of an animal is not like the sanctity of a human. This is the key point here.** We are not allowed to use this ruling on a human being, because that is murder. A human's life is not the same in the eyes of Allah as that of an animal. We do not bring about life and death for human beings; we leave it to Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. There is no mercy killing when it comes to human beings.

However, when it comes to animals, they do not occupy the same level of karamah, of sanctity, of nobility, as that of human beings. And if the owner of the animal, out of mercy for the animal, wishes to get rid of the misery of the animal and take the life of the animal, then the Shariah, or I should say the majority of scholars (I know there are always dissenting voices), would give that right, because it is the right of the animal's owner to take the life of the animal for a legitimate cause.

Our Shaykh Ibn Uthaymin said in his fatawa that if an animal becomes sick, and it is not one of those animals that you're allowed to eat, let's say a donkey, and you don't think that it's going to be cured, there is no sin if you kill the animal, because to keep the animal alive is actually spending extra time and money, and it's going to be painful to the animal. There's no point in doing that. So if an animal that is terminally sick is killed, there is no sin in this. And as for the animal that can be eaten, then it is permissible to actually expedite. Of course, in this case, obviously, if the cow is slightly sick or whatnot, you will expedite and then eat the animal, as long as the meat is not going to be spoiled or rotten because of that disease.

And of course other scholars as well: the famous Maliki scholar says in his Sharh of the Mukhtasar of Khalil that it is allowed to sacrifice that which is not eaten, such as a donkey or a mule, if it falls sick and it is about to die. In fact, he says it is encouraged to do that, in order to save that animal pain. This is a classical scholar in medieval Islam, and he is saying that when the animal is sick and it's about to die, it's in pain, it is recommended to get it out of its misery and to expedite this process.

And so, inshaAllah ta'ala, you are encouraged in this case. The doctors have said that it has cancer, so you are encouraged in this case to eliminate it from its cancer. And these days they have such a humane way of euthanizing. It's not like in those days; in those days it was a knife, and that's how they would get rid of it. These days it's much more humane, and the animal does not feel any pain.

And as for your question about Jannah, dear sister in Islam, or young sister in Islam: you work to get to Jannah, and inshaAllah, when you are in Jannah, they will have whatever they want in Jannah. So all of your desires and all of your hopes and all of your wishes will be satisfied in Jannah, and this animal of yours will be with you. The goal is that we have to make it to Jannah; we have to work to get there. May Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala make us of the people of Jannah.
